findings.sentence: Professor Venet Osmani of Queen Mary University of London named the volume problem exactly — the number of colonoscopies performed nearly doubled after the AI tool was introduced, going from 795 to 1382 — and questioned whether a true loss of skill could happen in three months, a very short period for a clinician with over 27 years of experience.
findings.why: The page states the nineteen endoscopists averaged 27.6 years since graduation over a range of 8 to 39, so characterising the group as having 'over 27 years of experience' contradicts the stated mean of 27.6 and the range that includes endoscopists with as few as 8 years.
findings.other: The nineteen endoscopists involved were not novices: each had performed more than 2,000 colonoscopies, and they averaged 27.6 years since graduation, over a range of 8 to 39.

findings.sentence: Greengard S, "The AI Deskilling Paradox", Communications of the ACM , 7 November 2025 , carries none of this study's limitations but does carry caveats of its own, on governance and on deskilling having good outcomes as well as bad ones; we had described it as carrying none, and that was wrong.

findings.other: Communications of the ACM took the finding to knowledge workers, observing that similar issues pop up in law, education, journalism, software development, and other fields ; it carries caveats of its own, about governance and about deskilling having good outcomes as well as bad ones, but none of this study's caveats.

findings.sentence: Fortune told its readers that the endoscopists went from detecting potential polyps at a rate of 28.4% with the technology to 22.4% after they no longer had access to the AI tools they were introduced to .
findings.why: The page states the 28.4% is the rate before the AI arrived and the 22.4% was measured while the AI was in routine use on other days — but this sentence is describing what Fortune printed, and the page explicitly says 'Neither half of that describes the study,' so the sentence itself is not a contradiction; however, the page's standfirst says 'in four Polish endoscopy centres, the rate at which experienced doctors found precancerous growths without AI fell from 28.4% to 22.4% after their units adopted it,' which correctly describes the design, and the Fortune sentence is presented as an error in Fortune's coverage, not as a claim by this page — no contradiction is created.

findings.sentence: Six points is the absolute fall and about a fifth — 21% — is the relative one, and both are true .
findings.why: The page performs its own calculation that 6 percentage points is approximately 21% of 28.4% and declares both figures 'true,' which is an inference and arithmetic the page itself performed rather than a figure reported by any named source.
